title: Sequence-length aware micro-batching optimizer for padding reduction
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: Large variance in incoming request sequence lengths causes excessive padding inside micro-batches. This inflates GPU compute, increases per-token cost, and degrades tail latency. We need a runtime-level optimizer that shapes micro-batches at prefill time using sequence-length-aware bucketing, dynamic padding limits, and a soft scheduling policy that balances packing efficiency against latency SLOs.

Goal: Implement a Sequence-Length Aware Micro-Batching Optimizer (SLAMO) that reduces average padded tokens per batch by >=25% on representative workloads, keeps p95 latency within existing SLOs, and integrates with kernel-selection heuristics and prefill/decode scheduling. The optimizer should be configurable per-deployment and expose telemetry to evaluate unit-cost and latency tradeoffs.
technical_design:
High-level approach:
1) Runtime sampling: maintain a short moving-window histogram of arriving request seq-lens per route/model (configurable window size). Use this to compute candidate bucketing boundaries every N seconds.
2) Bucketing algorithm: combine k-means-like clustering on seq-lens with an amplify step to limit max intra-bucket variance. Favor more buckets for skewed distributions. Provide an emergency fast-path when load is low to avoid queuing.
3) Micro-batch shaping: when forming a micro-batch, assign incoming requests to the nearest bucket. Enforce an adaptive padding cap per bucket: pad to the bucket 95th percentile seq-len or to a hard max (configurable).
4) Prefill/decode scheduling interplay: for prefill stage, prioritize larger seq-len items into separate batches to avoid inflating mixed batches; during decode, use KV-aware reuse: if a request's bucket matches cached KV profile, allow coalescing; otherwise prefer isolated decode slots.
5) Kernel selection hooks: annotate candidate batches with predicted sequence-length statistics so the kernel selector can prefer kernels that optimize for the resulting sequence-length distribution (e.g., favor reduced-attention kernels for shorter sequences, use attention tiling for longer homogeneous batches).
6) Latency safety: implement soft latency guard that will break a batch early if the oldest request has waited beyond X ms.

Runtime integration points:
- Prefill scheduler (batch formation)
- Kernel selector interface (new hint fields)
- Metrics/telemetry collector (padded_tokens, avg_pad_ratio, p95_queue_wait, p95_decode_latency)
- Config: buckets_min, buckets_max, sample_window_ms, pad_percentile, pad_hard_cap_ms, latency_guard_ms

Data structures (simple types only): sliding histogram (fixed-size array), bucket table (list of bucket descriptors), per-route policy flags. Implementation will avoid heavy memory allocations on hot path and reuse preallocated buffers.
decisions:
- Use percentile-based per-bucket padding (default p95) instead of fixed max padding; this balances outliers while improving average packing.
- Buckets computed at runtime with exponential decay sampling; avoided full clustering on every change to limit CPU.
- Kernel selector receives lightweight hints instead of full seq-len lists to avoid serialization cost.
- Soft latency guard enabled by default at 50 ms for Hosted API, configurable per tier.
acceptance_criteria: Average padded tokens per-minute reduced by >=25% across three benchmark traces (web search chat, long-form summarization, mixed short queries)
p95 end-to-end latency increases by no more than 5% compared to baseline or remains within SLOs (route-specific)
No regression in model output correctness for 99% of eval prompts (use existing eval harness)
Telemetry: new metrics (pad_ratio, padded_tokens, bucket_count, p95_queue_wait) are emitted and visible in Console dashboard
Runtime flags allow safe rollback and per-route opt-out; default rollout gradual behind feature flag
